label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.3 a.5…: If GOD_4 were properly in some genus, that genus…
locator: I q.3 a.5 co., second proof: si Deus esset in aliquo genere, oporteret quod genus eius esset ens
interpretation: Read as stated, for God: if God were in a genus, that genus would be being. Aquinas' reasons (God's esse is his essence, q.3 a.4; a genus signifies the essence, being said in quid) are not formalized and the statement is not generalized to every being whose esse is its essence; that generalization would need its own claim.
